OR B.

Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering.

The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure - Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico.

Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration.

Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. 3.

Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program. 4.

Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance.

Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions.

In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes assisting in the design of electrical engineering equipment or systems using established criteria or specifications; or, monitoring testing of electrical engineering systems to ensure proper functionality; or, identifying problems and recommending corrective action to electrical engineering systems.

This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-05). OR Education: One full year of graduate level education in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Engineering.

OR Superior Academic Achievement: Successful completion of all the requirements for a bachelor's degree with Superior Academic Achievement (S.A.A.).

In order to be creditable under this provision, Superior Academic Achievement must have been gained in a curriculum that is qualifying for the position to be filled, such as that identified in Education above.

Superior Academic Achievement is based on: (1) Class Standing - Applicants must be in the upper third of the graduating class in the college, university, or major subdivision, such as the College of Liberal Arts or the School of Business Administration, based on completed courses; OR (2) Grade-Point Average (G.P.A.) - Applicants must have a grade-point average of either (a) 3.0 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B" or better) as recorded on your official transcript, or as computed based on 4 years of education, or as computed based on courses completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum; or (b) 3.5 or higher out of a possible 4.0 ("B+" or better) based on the average of the required courses completed in the major field or the required courses in the major field completed during the final 2 years of the curriculum.; OR(3) Honor Society Membership - Applicants may be considered eligible based on membership in one of the approved national scholastic honor societies listed by the Association of College Honor Societies (https://www.achshonor.org/).

NOTE: Grade point averages will be rounded to one decimal point. For example, 2.95 will round to 3.0, and 2.94 will round to 2.9.

NOTE: If more than 10 percent of your undergraduate course work (credit hours) was taken on a pass/fail or similar basis, your S.A.A. claim must be based on class standing or membership in an honor society and you must provide evidence of your class standing or honor society membership with your application.

OR 5-Year Engineering Program: Successful completion of a 5-year program of study (i.e., one designed to be completed in no less than 5 years) of at least 160 semester hours leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering in an ABET accredited college or university.

OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12.

Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) by 18. Add the two percentages.

Job Description Summary: The Substation Engineer is responsible for the design, implementation, and supporting testing of electrical substation, ensuring they meet safety standards, operational requirements, and project specifications.

The Senior Substation Engineer should have a solid understanding of power systems, substation equipment, and relevant industry standards. This role is fully remote. Specific location details and expectations will be discussed during the interview process.

Job Description: * This job description reflects management's assignment of essential functions; it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned Position Responsibilities and Duties:
Design/Review electrical substations, including layout, equipment selection, and equipment specifications in accordance with project requirements and industry standards.
Review load flow, short circuit, and relay coordination studies to ensure the reliability and efficiency of substation designs.
Review detailed engineering drawings, schematics, and technical specifications using AutoCAD electrical or Bluebeam.
Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders, including utility companies, contractors, and regulatory agencies to obtain approvals and permits for substation projects.
Review and evaluate vendor proposals for technical accuracy to specifications for substation components.
Identify opportunities for design upgrades, improvements, or provide value engineering solutions.
Provide technical support during the construction, testing, and commissioning of new substations, ensuring compliance with project schedules and quality standards.
Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues related to substation equipment and systems, both remotely and on-site.
Perform root cause analysis and recommend corrective actions for substation failures.
Stay informed about emerging technologies and best practices in substation design, automation, and protection systems.
Assist in the development of standards, procedures, and guidelines for substation engineering activities.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including transmission planners, business development, testing and commissioning, construction, SCADA/OTS engineering, PV engineering, and BESS engineering to ensure the seamless integration of substations into the overall power grid.
Participate in constructability reviews and inspections to identify and mitigate potential hazards in substation facilities.
Assist with mentoring junior engineers, technicians, and peers providing guidance, training, and lessons learned on substation design principles and practices.
Maintain accurate documentation and records of substation designs and modifications.
Participate in team meetings/calls regularly
Demonstrate and maintain a safe work environment and direct safe work practices in energized substations.

In short If you're a firmware engineer who's just as comfortable reading a schematic as writing C, and you've spent serious time inside ESP32 or STM32 projects, we want to talk. You'd join us on a freelance , time & material basis : you're paid for the hours you actually work on real client projects.

The first three months are about figuring out if we're a good match. When things work out, and that depends on the work itself, the project pipeline, and business timing, there's a real path to our core team with a permanent contract and full benefits. Why intent ? We've been designing and co-creating connected devices since 2008.

Wearables, smart audio, health-tech hardware for clients like Oura and BOSE, backed by investors like a16z and Founders Fund. We're 60+ people, fully remote, and AI-native since before LinkedIn influencers discovered the term. Firmware is where most of our products actually live or die: BLE stacks, power budgets, sensor pipelines, OTA.

If you like the kind of bug that only shows up at -10°C with a flat battery, you'll feel at home. Who this role is NOT for If you like being told exactly what to flash every morning and logging off the second the linker finishes, we're probably not your people.

We look for engineers who ask "why" before "how", challenge assumptions, and dig into the hardware when the symptoms don't add up. We're AI-native and we expect you to treat AI as a daily multiplier, not a gimmick.

What we expect: ownership of what you touch, straight talk when something on the board doesn't behave, and the kind of curiosity that makes you actually care about the device, not just the code that ships to it. What you'll do
Plan, develop, and ship firmware for connected devices: wearables, audio, health-tech hardware
Gather and analyze requirements from clients, then turn them into something that actually works on real silicon
Consult clients and internal teams on stacks, tools, and trade-offs
Work side by side with mobile, backend, and QA to make sure the device and its companion app actually understand each other over BLE
Test firmware releases and write the documentation that future-you will thank present-you for
Estimate your own work and flag risks before they become blockers
Push for better practices: code reviews, patterns, knowledge-sharing inside and outside the chapter
Use AI tools as part of your daily workflow, not as a party trick
How we work Fully remote. We have a pet-friendly office in Warsaw and a coworking space in Gdansk if walls and coffee machines motivate you, but nobody will ask why you're not there. Working hours are flexible: most of the team operates between 10:00 and 18:00 CET, and that's when most meetings happen.

Evening calls with US-based clients (up to ~20:00) are part of the rhythm, sometimes a couple of times a week, always planned ahead. You'll be part of the Firmware & Hardware chapter for knowledge-sharing, and at the same time on a project squad led by a PM for day-to-day delivery. What you'll get

s.h: Truly flexible hours: you organize your day
s.t:
Fully remote, with pet-friendly Warsaw office + Gdansk cowork if you want them
Access to our internal knowledge-sharing: tech talks, experiments, side projects
When the first 3 months work out, and that depends on the work, the project pipeline, and business timing, there's a real path to a permanent contract with a fixed monthly salary, 26 days paid leave, 10 sick days, Saltus medical care, and a training budget
No sugarcoating: during the freelance period there's no paid leave or medical benefits. Those come with the permanent contract, and we're transparent about that upfront.

Your first weeks We aim to give you space to ramp up before jumping into live project work, but this is a real company with real deadlines: if the project needs you sooner, we'll make sure you have the support to hit the ground running.

You'll get paired with a technical buddy and tackle progressively bigger tasks, so both sides can see how the collaboration feels. Feedback comes early and often, no one waits three months to tell you something isn't working. If it's great, you'll know. If something needs adjusting, you'll hear about it while there's still time to adjust.

Recruitment process The entire process is in English. All interviews are recorded for internal evaluation purposes.
Application with a few screening questions
HR call, ~45 min, casual
Technical meeting, ~90 min, with the firmware team
Final feedback within a few days
Once we're in touch, you'll hear from us fast. We don't ghost and we don't drag. One more thing intent is an equal opportunity employer. We care about what you can do, not where you come from. Send us your CV and a few words about why this caught your eye. Bonus points if you share something you've built that made you proud, ideally something where the firmware had to behave under conditions nobody told you about upfront. Requirements What we're looking for
4+ years of professional firmware development
Strong C/C++ for embedded systems (not "I dabbled in microcontrollers in school")
Hands-on ESP32 experience, including ESP-IDF and ESP-ADF
STM32 experience in production projects
Solid Bluetooth knowledge: BLE, Bluetooth Mesh, and comfort across the stack layers
Toolchain fluency: CMake, GCC, Python-based tooling
Familiarity with IoT protocols like MQTT and WebSockets
A feel for the connected device landscape: IoT, home automation, wearables, automotive
English at B2+, written and spoken, because our clients are mostly US-based
Self-reliance, ownership, and the kind of communication where people don't have to guess what you meant

Rapid hardware prototyping on Arduino, Raspberry Pi, BeagleBone, Nucleo
Working knowledge of LoRa, Zigbee, Thread, Wi-Fi, and other networking standards
Fleet deployment and management with AWS IoT Core, GCP Cloud IoT, Azure IoT, or similar
Cryptography in embedded contexts
Audio paths: encoding, decoding, mixers
Machine learning on embedded targets
Rust in firmware
FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or other embedded operating systems
Genuine curiosity about the devices you build, not just the bits flying around them

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit and that can carry cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.
We are looking for a passionate and experienced Automation/Electrical Engineer to join our HiL/EGSE Engineering Team in Munich. You will contribute to the design, development, and integration of complex Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) platforms , supporting the verification and validation of avionics and electrical subsystems.
These platforms are composed of hundreds of electrical and electronic components (both COTS and custom-made) and must meet CE marking and Machinery Directive compliance. Your work will have a direct impact on the performance, reliability, and safety of critical aerospace systems.

In your role as an Automation/Electrical Engineer for HiL Platform Development, you will be responsible for the following:
Lead the compliant design of electrical schematics for both power and signal circuits
Define and implement safety devices, protection mechanisms, and power management solutions
Be responsible for the overall electrical design of the HiL test laboratory
Develop and support electrical setups for component and subsystem testing — ranging from simple rigs to highly integrated systems
Ensure compliance with industry standards , CE marking, and applicable electrical safety regulations
Collaborate with a highly skilled cross-functional team (software, simulation, mechanical, avionics) throughout the development lifecycle
Participate in technical reviews , support documentation efforts, and ensure traceability of requirements
Occasionally travel abroad to support customers, suppliers, or company affiliates

s.h: You and your team will be in charge of
s.t:
Defining the architecture of HiL electrical systems , ensuring scalability, reliability, and maintainability
Selecting, specifying, and integrating electrical components and interfaces for the test platforms
Performing make-or-buy analysis , managing suppliers and coordinating with procurement
Supporting the integration of real-time simulation environments and electrical interfaces (e.g., power supplies, loads, relays, sensors, signal conditioning)
Contributing to risk assessments and FMEAs related to electrical design
Driving continuous improvement to increase the safety, efficiency, and modularity of test platforms
What we would love to see from you

s.h: Ideally, you bring the following experience and qualifications
s.t:
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical, Electronic, or Automation Engineering
Strong understanding of electrical system design , circuit protection, and signal integrity
Solid knowledge of industry standards and regulations (e.g., IEC/EN standards, Machinery Directive, CE marking)
Experience using electrical CAD tools (e.g., EPLAN, Zuken, or equivalent) for schematic design and documentation
Knowledge of electronic circuit design (analog and digital) is a plus
Experience working in aerospace, automotive, or industrial automation is highly desirable
Familiarity with HiL testing , test bench architecture, or EGSE systems is a plus
Excellent problem-solving skills and a pragmatic, cost-conscious design mindset
Fluent in English (spoken and written); German is a plus
Why you should join us!
What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:
We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind
We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them
We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?

## **Ta mission :** ##
**Concevoir et modéliser des plans techniques de qualité**
Vous réalisez, adaptez et optimisez les plans d-installations électriques à l-aide d-AutoCAD et Revit. Vous produisez une documentation technique précise, fiable et conforme aux normes suisses ainsi qu-aux exigences spécifiques de chaque projet.
**Garantir la fiabilité des données techniques**
Vous utilisez Winprogitel avec rigueur afin d-assurer la cohérence, l-exactitude et la mise à jour des données techniques nécessaires au bon déroulement des études et à la réalisation des installations.
**Contrôler et valider les documents d-exécution**
Vous vérifiez les plans, schémas et documents techniques afin de garantir leur conformité aux cahiers des charges, aux réglementations en vigueur et aux contraintes opérationnelles du terrain.
**Participer à la coordination des projets**
En étroite collaboration avec les chefs de projet, architectes, ingénieurs et équipes de réalisation, vous contribuez à la coordination des études, à l-anticipation des contraintes techniques et à la recherche de solutions adaptées.
**Assurer le suivi de l-avancement des études**
Vous assurez un suivi régulier des projets, communiquez sur leur progression et veillez à la bonne prise en compte des ajustements nécessaires afin de respecter les objectifs de qualité, de délais et de performance.
**Contribuer à l-amélioration continue**
Force de proposition, vous participez activement à l-optimisation des méthodes de travail, à l-évolution des outils de conception et à l-amélioration continue de la qualité des livrables techniques.
**Votre contribution**
Grâce à votre expertise en conception, votre maîtrise des outils de dessin technique et votre sens du détail, vous jouez un rôle essentiel dans la réussite des projets en garantissant des études fiables, cohérentes et parfaitement exécutables sur le terrain
## **Maintenant si on parlait de toi ?** ##
**Une formation spécialisée en planification électrique**
Vous êtes titulaire d-un CFC de planificateur-électricien ou d-une formation jugée équivalente. Cette formation vous a permis d-acquérir de solides compétences en conception, dimensionnement et planification d-installations électriques conformes aux normes.
**Une expérience reconnue sur le marché suisse**
Vous justifiez d-au moins 2 ans d-expérience professionnelle en Suisse dans la planification ou l-étude d-installations électriques. Vous maîtrisez les spécificités du marché local, les exigences réglementaires ainsi que les contraintes techniques liées aux différents types de projets.
**Une parfaite maîtrise des outils de conception**
Vous utilisez avec aisance AutoCAD, Revit et Winprogitel pour élaborer des plans détaillés, produire une documentation technique de qualité et assurer un suivi rigoureux des études tout au long des projets.
**Rigueur et précision technique**
Méthodique et attentif aux détails, vous analysez, contrôlez et validez les documents d-exécution avec exigence. Votre sens de la qualité vous permet de garantir des livrables fiables, conformes et parfaitement exploitables par les équipes de réalisation.
**Un véritable esprit collaboratif**
Vous appréciez le travail en équipe et savez collaborer efficacement avec les chefs de projet, ingénieurs, architectes et équipes de chantier. Votre capacité à communiquer clairement favorise la coordination et la réussite des projets.
**Autonomie et sens des responsabilités**
Organisé et proactif, vous savez gérer vos priorités, anticiper les besoins et proposer des solutions adaptées aux enjeux techniques rencontrés. Vous faites preuve d-initiative tout en respectant les objectifs fixés.
**Mobilité et engagement**
Titulaire du permis de conduire catégorie B, vous êtes disposé à effectuer des déplacements sur les chantiers et auprès des différents intervenants afin d-assurer un suivi efficace et une bonne coordination des projets.
**Ce qui fera la différence**
Votre maîtrise des outils de conception, votre rigueur technique et votre capacité à collaborer avec l-ensemble des acteurs du projet font de vous un véritable partenaire de confiance dans la réussite des études et la qualité des réalisations.

The successful candidate will perform the full range of Fire Protection Engineer duties.

Such duties include but are not limited to: Reviewing and evaluating, regarding the safety consequences of fire, applications for source and special nuclear material licenses, safety analysis reports, and environmental reports for fuel cycle facilities engaged in nuclear fuel fabrication, chemical processing of nuclear materials, enrichment, scrap recovery, and waste processing.

Recommending and developing NRC policy and assists in the drafting of regulations, standards, procedures, and guides governing the Commission's regulatory program.

Evaluating, regarding fire safety, the applicant's technical qualifications, including the training and experience of the members of the applicant's staff, to operate nuclear facilities in a manner that protects public health and the environment and minimizes danger to life and property.

Evaluating licensee administrative programs, staffing, procedures, and equipment for adequacy of identification, assessment, mitigation, and monitoring of fire hazards. Making recommendations to management on programs and approaches needed to develop and maintain effective NRC fire safety policies, regulations, guidance, and programs.

Makes professional presentations to other Agency offices as necessary to ensure effective communication. Preparing technical reports, documents, and publications as necessary to promote, support, and describe the NRC fire safety program.

Maintaining technical knowledge of the fire hazards of licensed facility operations and identifies needed research work to appropriately understand and address any special issues that may arise. Advises management on matters involving application of fire safety principles to complex processes and equipment.

Preparing written reports or technical publications, such as safety evaluation reports and environmental assessments, regarding the results of the evaluations and analyses which set forth the incumbent's conclusions and/or recommendations tor licensing action.

Communicating with NRC staff and management, licensees, other Federal agencies, State and local officials, media, and members of the public regarding fire safety. Prepares responses to inquiries about Congressional, public, and others' concerns in matters of fuel cycle safety.
In order to qualify for this position, you must have at least one year of specialized experience at the next lower grade level in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE is defined as: Knowledge and/or experience as a technical expert reviewer for fire safety aspects of licensing applications for nuclear fuel cycle facilities; knowledge of fire protection programs and the effects of fires/explosions on structures, systems, and components that are important to safety; experience in developing safety evaluation reports; and experience in developing policy, standards, and guidance.

The ideal candidate will be able to demonstrate the following: Demonstrated knowledge of Fire Protection Engineering Expertise for Nuclear Fuel Cycle Facilities. Demonstrated ability to perform Licensing Review, Regulatory Compliance, and Technical Documentation.

Demonstrated experience with Integrated Hazard Analysis and Interdisciplinary Coordination. Demonstrated experience with Policy, Standards, Guidance, and Rulemaking Support. Demonstrated experience with Communication, Stakeholder Engagement, and Expert Testimony.

A description of how you possess the specialized experience as well as how you meet the qualifications desired in an ideal candidate must be addressed in your resume. Applicants may also use the supplemental vacancy question to provide additional information pertaining to the specialized experience and ideal candidate criteria.

Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!
Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.
We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.
It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.
🐙 Kraken Generation Flex
The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In the UK, with a legally binding Net Zero target for 2050 and a clean-power ambition for 2030, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.
Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. With complete independence from Octopus Energy, we are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As our UK fleet grows and we support our expansion across Europe, we are looking for an Integrations Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets.

s.h: 🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary
s.t:
As we scale our fleet of integrated assets, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing.
You’ll be part of an engineering delivery team, based in Manchester, who take an integration project from the very early information stage, design how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turn that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset.
Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing; they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing.
🚀 What you'll own
Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches. When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members.
Technical judgement: Develop your technical judgement, making well-reasoned decisions and trade-offs with support from senior engineers, and contributing technical input to discussions within the team.
Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include grid regulations (G99, G100, Grid Code etc.), energy markets, multi BMUs, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on.
Gateway application & configuration: Learn how the Gateway software (developed by an internal software team) works and how it is configured. Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time.
Hardware and Software Deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing with guidance from the senior engineers.
Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team.
Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand grows.
Incidents & compliance: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites.

s.h: 🧠 What you'll bring to the party
s.t:
Understanding of the Regulations: Working knowledge of the UK Grid Code, G99 and the other obligations of a grid-connected asset before it can participate in the energy markets.
Understanding of the UK Energy Markets: Working understanding of the NESO ancillary services (Dynamic Containment / Moderation / Regulation, Firm Frequency Response), the Balancing Mechanism, and the DNO connection/integration process.
Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution.
Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation.
Asset integration: Exposure to, or a keen interest in, integrating BESS (grid-scale and/or C&I) and/or RES (Wind and Solar) for telemetry and control.
Integration design: Ability to contribute to clear integration designs and design documentation.
Hardware and Networking: Familiarity with control systems deployments and their connectivity including the local networking and cyber security aspects, and an ability to help debug site connectivity and networking issues (including 4G routers and firewalls) with support.
Industrial Communication Protocols: Practical experience or a good working knowledge of Modbus (TCP/RTU); awareness of one or more of IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25, OPC-UA or DNP3 is a plus.
CAD, Diagrams and Tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion.
Communication: A clear communicator who documents their work (e.g. in design docs and Notion) and collaborates well with the team.
Commissioning landscape: Awareness of the other parties involved in site commissioning for power plants, their roles and responsibilities, and how we work with them.
Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, Software, or a related field - or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration.
A proactive and collaborative mindset: You are eager to learn and grow, reliable and collaborative. You take initiative, communicate openly, raise risks early, and care about safe working. You welcome feedback, support your teammates, and steadily build toward taking on more independent ownership of integrations over time.
Travel: Willingness to travel to customers and sites although travel is very occasional. Awareness of site safety is required as we may work with site personnel even though we are remote.

**Technik verstehen. Menschen führen. Sicherheit leben.**

Sie verbinden technisches Verständnis mit Führungsstärke, analytischem Denken und Verantwortungsbewusstsein.
Sie behalten auch bei komplexen Fragestellungen den Überblick, gehen Ursachen auf den Grund, entwickeln nachhaltige Lösungen und bringen gemeinsam mit Ihrem Team Verbesserungen voran.

* Sie führen mit Klarheit und Wertschätzung, entwickeln Mitarbeitende weiter und bringen Ihre Eigeninitiative auch bei der Weiterentwicklung bestehender Abläufe ein.
